packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 18 - unverified image-only reading

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification
or earlier reading of this item. I did not read packet.json. One thing beyond
the strict rules: I ran a single directory listing of the three packet
directories to learn the image filenames (filenames and sizes only).

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001, overview)
- Observation: inside of a book board (grey pasteboard, parchment turn-ins),
  with a ruler. Along the gutter a narrow vertical parchment strip (binding
  guard / hinge reinforcement), about 1.5-2 cm wide, carries writing. Text runs
  horizontally in the normal upright orientation, in short line-ends/line-
  fragments: only some 12-20 letters of each line survive, so every line is a
  fragment of a much wider column. Which margin of the original column is
  preserved cannot be told from the crop.
- Observation: tiny, heavily abbreviated cursive in brown ink. The writing is
  in separate blocks divided by blank bands (at least six blocks down the
  strip); no rubric, no enlarged initial, no running title, no underlining
  seen. Sewing-support slots/thongs interrupt the strip at three points.
- Tentative interpretation: the blank bands may be paragraph breaks, or the
  blocks may be separate short notes/glosses (e.g. marginal apparatus cut from
  beside a main text). Not decidable from this strip.
- image-005 is a second overview (see below).

Tiles are only c. 276 px wide; letter forms are at the limit of resolution.
Almost every reading below is uncertain; I mark the more doubtful ones with ?
but the whole should be treated as low-confidence.

--- image-002 (strip, upper part; blocks 1 and 2, start of 3) ---
Block 1

=====================================================================
SECOND FACE / SECOND STRIP (image-005 overview; tiles 006-009)

LAYOUT (image-005)
- Observation: same volume, view of the spine (raised bands, damaged covering)
  and inner board. A narrow written parchment strip lies along the joint at the
  left, same hand and ink as the strip in image-001; it is slightly wider here
  (about 2.5 cm) and better preserved. Text again in separate blocks divided by
  blank bands: I count four blocks in the small script, then at the foot a
  series of short entries in a larger, looser hand (different ink strokes).
- Observation: at least three of the four small-script blocks begin with the
  same sign, an "h"-like letter with a stroke (read below as "h(ic)"?), set at
  the left edge. The left edge of these blocks therefore looks like a real line
  beginning; the right ends are cut or run into the fold.
- Tentative interpretation: a run of short section-by-section notes, each
  opening "h(ic) ..." ("here he ...") and reporting what a text says or
  posits (verbs like "po(n)it", "d(ici)t", "declarat" seem to recur). This is
  an inference from repeated openings, not from a visible lemma or heading.
  No rubric, initial, underlining or running title is visible.

--- image-006 (block A, top; start of block B at foot) ---
Block A

(long blank band, with a brown stain)

--- image-007 (block B complete; start of block C) ---
Block B
image-007 L1:  h(ic)(?) po(n)it(?) aliu(m) mo(dum) d(icen)di(?) (et) u[...]

--- image-008 (rest of block C; block D) ---

Block C continued

--- image-009 (end of block D; later entries in a larger hand) ---
image-009 L1-5 repeat image-008 L25-29 (overlap).
Below, after a gap, about twelve short entries in a larger, looser, greyer
hand, one or two words each, set at irregular intervals; the left edge is
partly under the fold. They look like jottings or pen trials, possibly
repeating key words of the notes above. Readings are very uncertain:
image-009 L6:  [..] (con)iu(n)g(?)[..]
image-009 L7:  [..] q(?)[..] simul(?)
image-009 L8:  color(?)
image-009 L9:  [..] p(ro)ba(n)t(?) (a horizontal stroke runs through the word:
               deletion or flourish)
image-009 L10: [..] mo(do)(?)
image-009 L11: [..] bap(?)[..]
image-009 L12: [..] iuxtapo(s)it(?)[..]
image-009 L13: [..] q(?)[..]
image-009 L14: [..] iuxtapo(?)[..] vide(?)
image-009 L15: [..] ad mediu(m)(?)
image-009 L16: [..] iuxtapo(?)[..]
image-009 L17: color(?)
image-009 L18: [..] gi[..]

AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
- Attempted: every block on both strips. Best-read spans are blocks A-D of
  the second strip (image-006 to -008); the first strip (image-002 to -004)
  yielded only scattered words.
- Words I am reasonably confident recur on the second strip: "color",
  "colorum", "delectabile/delectabiles", "sonorum", "melodye", "visus/visum",
  "apparet", "confuse ad sensum/visum", "minima", "opinio", "radios ... a
  visu". On the first strip: "de origine", "declarat", "2o"/"3o" as ordinals.
- Unread or effectively unread: first strip blocks 5 and 6; much of first
  strip blocks 1-4; the right-hand ends of all lines (cut or in the fold).

LIMITATIONS AND SUGGESTIONS
- Tiles are native resolution but the script is only a few pixels high, so
  minims and abbreviation strokes cannot be counted; expansions in parentheses
  are proposals, and several whole-word readings (e.g. "iuxtapositio",
  "defluxionem", "proportione", "contactum") rest on word shape only.
- Every line is truncated on at least one side; the two strips may be from
  the same or different leaves, and their order is unknown. Whether the two
  strips are two faces of one piece or two separate pieces cannot be told.
- A higher-magnification capture of the strips (or raking light for first
  strip blocks 5-6) would be needed for a continuous transcription.
- This is an unverified image reading.
